claim: Firms may consider costs incurred in providing the product, market rates for comparable products, and benefits when assessing fair value.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: A manufacturer may consider one or more of the following in its assessment of whether or not a product is providing fair value: (1) the costs incurred by the firm in manufacturing or distributing the product; (2) the market rate and charges for a comparable product; (3) any accrued costs and/or benefits for existing or closed products; and (4) whether there are any products that are priced significantly lower for a similar or better benefit.

claim: Firms can consider their expected costs over the lifetime of the product, including the cost of financing, when assessing fair value.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: So, for example, lenders can take account of the costs of providing credit when assessing fair value, including the cost of the financing behind the credit.

claim: For consumer credit products, firms must consider all interest, fees and charges a consumer may incur, including late payment/arrears charges.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: For example, for consumer credit products, like personal loans or credit cards, firms must consider all interest, fees and charges a consumer may incur, including late payment/ arrears charges.

claim: Firms must design and deliver support that meets the needs of customers, including those with characteristics of vulnerability, ensure customers can use products as reasonably anticipated, avoid unreasonable barriers, monitor support quality, and not disadvantage vulnerable customer groups.

llm_check.supporting_sentence:
They require firms to:
• design and deliver support that meets the needs of customers, including those 
with characteristics of vulnerability
• ensure that customers can use their products as reasonably anticipated
• ensure they include appropriate friction in customer journeys to mitigate the risk 
of harm and give customers sufficient opportunity to understand and assess their 
options, including any risks
• ensure that customers do not face unreasonable barriers (including unreasonable 
additional costs) during the lifecycle of a product or service
• monitor the quality of the support they are offering, looking for evidence that may 
indicate areas where they fall short of the outcome, and act promptly to address 
these, and
• ensure they do not disadvantage particular groups of customers, including those 
with characteristics of vulnerability

claim: Firms should have exceptions processes to deal with non-standard issues such as fraud or financial difficulty, likely requiring a real-time human interface, must make reasonable adjustments for disabled customers, and must support customers whose needs change (including helping them exit a product), as well as maintain operational resilience of support.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: Firms should also have exceptions processes in place to deal effectively with non‑standard issues that could arise in the context of their business.

claim: Firms must monitor the quality of consumer support delivered and take prompt remedial action, including where support is outsourced, where it falls short of expectations.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: Where a firm’s consumer support is provided by an outsourced third party, either in whole or in part, we expect the firm to have systems and processes in place to monitor that the support meets the standard set out under this outcome.

claim: Firms are not required to offer multiple channels, but must ensure the channel(s) offered meet customer needs and respond flexibly to vulnerable circumstances, and must deal promptly and fairly with support failures, including providing redress.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: Firms should however provide support that meets the needs of their customer base and target market.

claim: Firms must ensure product design meets the needs, characteristics and objectives of customers in the identified target market, that distribution strategy is appropriate, and that regular reviews are carried out to ensure continued fit.

llm_check.supporting_sentence:
They set out a range of requirements, including the need for relevant firms to:
• ensure that the design of the product or service meets the needs, characteristics and objectives of customers in the identified target market
• ensure that the intended distribution strategy for the product or service is appropriate for the target market
• carry out regular reviews to ensure that the product or service continues to meet the needs, characteristics and objectives of the target market

claim: Firms should monitor that distribution strategies are followed and products reach the intended target market, using data to review whether products continue to meet customer needs.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: How is the firm monitoring that distribution strategies are being followed and that products and services are being correctly distributed to the target market?

claim: The products and services outcome does not require firms to ensure suitability for individual customers except in specific contexts like affordability assessments for loans, which are governed separately.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: Ensure that products or services are suitable for individual customers within the target market, except where this is relevant in the context. For example, firms need to consider suitability for individual customers when providing advice or discretionary services, or assess affordability when arranging a loan. Applicable rules regarding these activities continue to apply separately to the rules under this outcome, which are general in nature.

claim: Firms must present information logically, make key information prominent and easy to identify (e.g., via headings, layout, tables), and provide an appropriate level of detail to support effective decision-making.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: In supporting the understanding of retail customers through its communications, a firm should: (1) explain or present information in a logical manner; (2) use plain and intelligible language and, where use of jargon or technical terms is unavoidable, explain the meaning of any jargon or technical terms as simply as possible; (3) make key information prominent and easy to identify, including by means of headings and layout, display and font attributes of text, and by use of design devices such as tables, bullet points, graphs, graphics, audio-visuals and interactive media; (4) avoid unnecessary disclaimers; and (5) provide relevant information with an appropriate level of detail, to avoid providing too much information such that it may prevent retail customers from making effective decisions.

claim: Firms should help consumers navigate information by putting all information on a particular issue in one place or signposting/layering it so it is interlinked, rather than requiring consumers to piece together information from multiple documents.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: Firms should help consumers navigate the information they provide. For example, by putting all information on a particular issue in one place or signpost or layer it in a way so it is all interlinked.

claim: Firms must consider all costs and charges a consumer may pay for a product over time, including contingent charges like late payment fees.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: When considering the price charged, manufacturer firms must consider all the costs and charges a consumer may pay for the product or service over time.

claim: For consumer credit products like personal loans, firms must consider all interest, fees and charges a consumer may incur, including late payment/arrears charges.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: For example, for consumer credit products, like personal loans or credit cards, firms must consider all interest, fees and charges a consumer may incur, including late payment/ arrears charges.

claim: Firms must demonstrate that the total price paid, including fees and charges, represents fair value, and must not impose unreasonable exit charges.

llm_check.supporting_sentence:
As well as considering the fairness of interest rates 
charged, firms will need to be able to demonstrate that the total price paid for 
the product, including any fees and charges that they (or others) may apply, 
represents fair value.

claim: Firms can consider expected costs over the lifetime of the product, including the cost of providing credit, when assessing fair value in the round, alongside other Duty elements such as ability to exit.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: This makes clear that firms can consider their expected costs over the lifetime of the product as part of assessing fair value.

claim: Firms must respond flexibly to the needs of customers with characteristics of vulnerability, including by adapting their usual approach or offering different channels.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: We expect firms to respond flexibly to the needs of customers with characteristics of vulnerability. So, firms will usually need to be able to provide support to their customers through different channels or by adapting their usual approach.

claim: Firms should be mindful that anyone can become vulnerable temporarily or permanently and must have processes in place to prevent harm to these customers.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: Firms should also be mindful that anyone, including those who are tech‑savvy, can become vulnerable either temporarily or permanently.

claim: Consumer harm can arise from uncertainty around how or where to access support, so firms should ensure clear access points.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: uncertainty around how or where to access support, or poor hand-off processes, including where third parties are involved in its provision

claim: Firms must ensure product design meets the needs, characteristics and objectives of customers in the identified target market, that distribution strategy is appropriate for that target market, and that regular reviews are carried out to ensure the product continues to meet target market needs.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: They set out a range of requirements, including the need for relevant firms to: • ensure that the design of the product or service meets the needs, characteristics and objectives of customers in the identified target market • ensure that the intended distribution strategy for the product or service is appropriate for the target market • carry out regular reviews to ensure that the product or service continues to meet the needs, characteristics and objectives of the target market

claim: Firms must monitor whether distribution strategies are being followed and whether products continue to meet customers' needs.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: How is the firm monitoring that distribution strategies are being followed and that products and services are being correctly distributed to the target market?

claim: Manufacturers must ensure products are designed to meet the target market's needs, characteristics and objectives and avoid foreseeable harm to that market.

llm_check.supporting_sentence:
The rules require firms to ensure each product or service is designed:
• to meet the identified needs, characteristics and objectives of customers in the 
identified target market
• so that it does not adversely affect groups of customers in the target market, 
including groups with characteristics of vulnerability
• to avoid causing foreseeable harm to customers in the target market

claim: Firms must ensure consumers are given the information they need, at the right time, presented in a way they can understand, to support informed decision-making.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: We want customers to be given the information they need, at the right time, and presented in a way they can understand.

claim: Firms should develop an approach to testing communications to provide assurance that consumers can identify and understand the information needed to make effective decisions, including key features, costs, risks, and how to access support.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: Firms should develop an approach to testing that provides assurance that consumers can identify and understand the information needed to make effective decisions.

claim: The consumer understanding outcome applies broadly to all communications, including product terms and conditions, not just mandated disclosures.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: This outcome is also broader than other specific disclosure requirements and applies to all financial promotions, other advertisements and communications provided to consumers, including verbally – such as during conversations with advisers, online, in letters or product terms and conditions.

claim: Reliance on existing statutory disclosure requirements (such as those under the Consumer Credit Act 1974) alone may not be sufficient to meet the consumer understanding outcome, as such disclosures can be technical and inflexible.

llm_check.supporting_sentence: Disclosures prescribed under the Consumer Credit Act 197 4 (CCA) were regularly cited as being problematic due to their technical and inflexible nature.
